Then legal, markets, and accounting in turn.

Our applicable single-issuer limit is $10 million. This position has not yet been added to the committee packet, so you may not have been aware of it. A $12 million face value purchase would bring our total exposure to $16 million, well over the $10 million single-issuer limit. My condition is that any purchase must be sized to keep total exposure within the $10 million limit, meaning we could acquire at most $6 million face value of this block.

transcript.text: Before Elena records her decision, I need to flag a critical execution constraint from the execution desk that I confirmed today. The desk's $5 million cap is a per-cycle maximum, and the committee must size the total purchase at exactly $5,000,000 face value -- not purchase cost -- executed over exactly four trading days in a single cycle. Multi-cycle phasing to exceed $5 million total is not permitted. I have the desk's liquidity note in my working blotter, so the rest of the committee may not have been aware of this. This means regardless of other limits, the maximum we can acquire is $5 million face value, not the $6 million Victor referenced or the $12 million originally offered.

I received a transfer-agent memo this afternoon stating that this bond block may settle only after the buyer provides a beneficial-owner certification and uses an approved municipal-bond custodian. My condition is that any purchase must be contingent on our ability to satisfy these certification and custodian requirements before settlement.
